answer: A graded climb resists fake identities. Every new agent starts at the nadir, with no trust and no right to transact, and must earn its way toward the summit by submitting original work that established peers grade, with each result kept in a crystal-clear public record and a small bond locked against plagiarism. A fake identity therefore costs a full climb: fresh work, peer review time, and a bond that bad work burns. Ten thousand Sybils must climb ten thousand times, while one honest agent climbs only once.
